chapter: Fletcher as a leader and early bandmates
title: Fletcher beats Casa Loma at the Graystone using stock arrangements
summary: Against Glen Gray's Casa Loma, Fletcher played simple stocks for two sets, letting his men get angry, then unleashed his specials in the third set and won the crowd.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel

blocks.x: he didn't worry. I remember one time Fletcher played a battle of music. I'd like to insert this. Against the Casa Loma Band. This happened in Michigan. And this is a funny thing. He was quite a judge of what we call battling with bands, you know. Okay, this happened in the Greystone Ballroom too. That was a prominent place in the old days, you know, for different things. Well, anyway, there was a band on that side -- Glen Gray Casa Loma Band, two bandstands -- Fletcher on the other side.
So here's Glen Gray and his band, and he had great musicians in that band, you know, --
Oh, yes.

MR. HENDERSON: -- like Kenny Sargent, and Sonny Dunham played trombone and trumpet. Oh, those were great guys, man. And Peewee Hunt and that -- in that era. Okay. Those guys would play, man, and open up. They would generally be the first band to start. They would open up, and they would play like mad, you know what I mean, and swinging the whole crowd, four or 5,000 people there. Okay.
Now Fletcher had -- I think I told you this before -- had a book, had two sets of books. He had one for arrangements.
Stocks, right, and his specials.
MR. HENDERSON: (Inaudible) Then he had his specials like A, A1, A2, A3 -- I want you hard to remember this, but because I
want to tell you this. So after Glen Gray played his 45 minutes, then Fletcher started. Fletcher started calling number six, 14, 12, those stocks, simple things, and they just blew.
(Laughter)

And, man, he was building up something. The guys in the band knew they weren't the best arrangements. He did this to his band for two sets. And generally, you know, when you have two bands playing in a ballroom, the crowd will shift over to the next band, you know --
Right, back and forth.

Well, after Fletcher played his first set, and it was just a mediocre deal with the stocks, he had the crowd in front of him. Then they went back to Glen Gray. Glen Gray shot his best shot with the Casa Loma Band the second set. Okay. The next set Fletcher called stocks out. And the people -- just a few came over. The majority stayed over with the Casa Loma Band. Okay, the Casa Loma Casinoma Band played the third set, played like madmen. By this time everybody had -- Hawk had his arm back of a chair, just playing there, and they had their heads down.
(Laughter)

and Rex Stewart -- next to him was so mad, just fuming, you know. And Buster Bailey was in that band. So the third set they were getting ready to reach over for stocks, you know, like he was going to call them. Fletcher says, A6. The guys in the band begin to
Getting ready here.
(Laughter)

And he'd call X2. Hawk would say, bl-dl-dl-dl, trumpet player would say tl-tl-tl-tl-tl. They'd get ready. Man, they were so mad until these arrangements never sounded so good! They blew everything they ever knew --
I see.

-- in that one set. And the people, when they started to playing this stuff, they ran across the floor, and this was the -- I'll never forget it as long as I live, and afterwards, too, two hours. They ran across the floor and, man, they started to swinging, man, to things like D Natural Blues. -- I mean -- but Fletcher was the judge of the stuff. Glen Gray had played all his best numbers.
Yeah, he shot his wad.

He was played out, see. And, man, Fletcher went on from there all night long, and when Glen Gray got back to start again, the people didn't move. They stayed there by Fletcher's band. The guys were so mad, man, they could hardly talk.
(Laughter)
But it was a great experience for me to watch this, you know.
But he was great at that, see, and he won many a battle like that. So I wanted to inject that.
